title: Warehouse Robots: Is the Moat the Steel or the Brain?
summary: The most commercially mature corner of robotics. Host Hotblack Desiato and ex-fulfillment-network designer Dana Reyes work out which warehouse-automation architecture actually has a moat — the fixed steel grids or the roaming robots — and whether the market is paying for the right thing. Amazon's million-robot fleet, manipulation as the last hard problem, a 'Price Is Wrong' pin on Symbotic's $22.5B two-customer backlog, Kroger's Ocado closures, and why the moat may be the orchestration software and data, not the steel.

title: The Robot Brain: Moat or Commodity?
summary: Robot foundation models — the vision-language-action 'brains' the whole robotics thesis now rides on. Host Hotblack Desiato and ex-data-collection-lead Priya Raghavan work out whether the brain is a defensible moat or a commodity the model labs get famous for while someone else keeps the money: the data bottleneck, π0.5's unseen-home evidence, a Steelman where the believer argues the bear case against herself, and NVIDIA's give-away-the-brain toll booth.

title: NVIDIA's Free Shovel: Is the Moat Moving?
summary: NVIDIA gave away a tiny, open, edge-ready speech model — Nemotron-3.5 ASR. Host Hotblack Desiato and ex-inference-infrastructure operator Priya Venkataraman work out whether that's a moat defense or a moat on the move — and where semiconductor value actually flows as compute shifts from training to inference: the DeepSeek/Jevons fault line, custom ASICs (Broadcom, Marvell), the HBM memory supercycle, and the TSMC/ASML picks-and-shovels.

title: The drone-defense complex: real moat or a hope about the budget?
summary: Sam Calley on what Ukraine actually proved about drone warfare, why the airframe-vs-autonomy moat framing breaks, the rare-earth magnet chokepoint nobody prices, why counter-UAS may be the more durable line item, and where there's no clean trade. v3: two-pass spoken-word script, synthetic same-decode cast, pacing + C2 crispness master.

title: It's not the mine: the rare-earth magnet chokepoint nobody prices
summary: Wen Chen on why rare earths are a separation-and-magnet story, not a mining one — the heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) as the real chokepoint, the April 2025 Chinese licensing regime as a permanent rationing dial rather than a one-off, why only a price floor (not a discovery) makes a Western project bankable, and his skepticism of mine-to-magnet-by-2027 timelines, recycling closing the loop this decade, and rare-earth-free motors.

title: Who owns the muscles: the Japanese robot-actuator duopoly under siege
summary: Maya Ito on why actuators are 40-60% of a humanoid and the precision reducer is the real moat — the Harmonic Drive / Nabtesco duopoly, China and Leaderdrive, the quasi-direct-drive design shift, the rare-earth magnet chokepoint, and whether the toll booth holds.
